speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This supported his growth as a Student Leader, as he became more comfortable and confident when interacting with others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, Adam is in his school's student council executive committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: By providing students with opportunities to interact with a wider group of peers, Full SBB also helps us dissolve perceived boundaries between "them" and "us".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Fahrin from Fuhua Secondary School discovered the joy of meeting new people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Through these expanded connections, he now has formed a larger and more diverse network that he can draw support from.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Many of us in this House have spoken about the importance of nurturing a "we first" society, and we can start from our schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This is where our students learn to embrace diversity and contribute in different ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: It is where our students learn to grow, understand and empathise with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: It is where our children are instilled with our shared values.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: In this regard, grounding our students in core values and 21st Century Competencies is critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Values like resilience, respect and harmony, and civic, global and cross-cultural competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This forms the basis for openness, so we can know, understand and empathise with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: These values and competencies need to be lived, embodied and experienced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: To Mr Shawn Huang's suggestions, MOE has implemented moves to free up space for holistic development, while reducing an over-emphasis of academic results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: We want to teach less and learn more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This provides greater room for students to conduct student-led, self-directed exploration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: When mid-year exams were removed, teachers from Fuchun Primary School did not use the opportunity to cover more curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Instead, teachers thoughtfully designed lessons to weave in the development of 21st Century Competencies into students' learning experiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Under the school's signature Home Skills Programme, Primary 3 students worked together to make a healthy fruit salad by applying financial literacy concepts to plan within a budget, health education principles to understand the nutritional value of fruits, and adaptive thinking to design a salad that meets the needs of their grandparents or family members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Such authentic learning experiences transform subject knowledge into purposeful application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students used the time freed up from preparing for mid-year exams to deal with real-world problems in groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This provided the opportunity to strengthen the 21st Century Competencies of our Primary 3 children, including adaptive thinking and practicing responsible decision-making both at school and at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Beyond that, secondary schools and pre-university institutions have implemented Student-Initiated Learning (SIL), as a component of Home-Based Learning days.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Under SIL, time is set aside for students to pursue their interests and learn outside the curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: The intention is to encourage students to be more curious and self-directed in their learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: As part of students' holistic development, schools develop students as active contributors and concerned citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Schools encourage students to speak up and provide them with age-appropriate ways to participate in decision-making.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, some schools create official channels for students to suggest ways to better support their disadvantaged peers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Others also organise forums and townhalls where older students can discuss issues and ideas directly with the school management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: To support this, students are encouraged to start their own Values-in-Action projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Instead of just participating in school-planned community service, they design and they carry out their own projects to benefit the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Besides developing their planning and project management skills, such projects also help build active citizenship, empathy and leadership skills in our students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Azhar Othman suggested for primary and secondary schools to offer a non-examinable subject on entrepreneurship, to cultivate students who are innovative and creative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: We agree that as part of a holistic education, it is important to develop an enterprising spirit and innovating mindset.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Whether our students choose to become entrepreneurs or not, these qualities will help them to navigate their careers and life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This is why MOE prioritises the development of the 21st Century Competencies like critical, adaptive and inventive thinking skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: They are built through different subjects and school programmes such as Values-in-Action projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: The Applied Learning Programmes also help develop these competencies, particularly those that are focused on innovation, business and entrepreneurship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Beyond initiatives to build up students’ 21st Century Competencies, CCAs offer a regular platform for students to discover their interests, develop their talents and build strong character.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: In support of this, the Strategic Partnership CCA (SP-CCA) programme offers centralised, non-school-based CCAs to enable secondary school students to pursue activities beyond what their individual schools can provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students from different schools can come together, build friendships and support each other through the ups and downs of sporting experiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Through SP-CCA Athletics, she found herself training alongside Xavier from Fairfield Methodist School, and twins Jairus and Jayden from Woodlands Secondary School.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: What started as polite interactions during training blossomed into a supportive friendship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: They began meeting for lunch, did self-study together and supported each other in their sporting and academic pursuits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Their coaches shared that their friendship has brought positive energy to every training session.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: When we bring students together across school boundaries, we are not just developing athletic talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: We are bringing Singaporeans together to bond over shared experiences and interests, and to learn, grow and work together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: In doing so, we are nurturing relationships that will strengthen our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to do more in this space by offering and expanding SP-CCA opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: MOE and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) are committed to providing more avenues for our students to pursue their sporting passions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This is in line with MOE’s efforts to ensure that students can benefit from regular physical activity and are supported from a well-being perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Gerald Giam suggested to increase minimum Physical Education (PE) curriculum time in primary schools to five hours weekly, and Mr Dennis Tan proposed later school start times to prioritise students’ sleep health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong also suggested for school classrooms to have indoor temperature standards and mixed-mode air-conditioning to facilitate learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: I will first share about MOE's current efforts in these areas, before addressing Members’ suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, MOE schools adopt a holistic approach to encourage active and healthy lifestyles, as well as good sleep health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This is comparable to most other systems internationally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Through PE lessons, students learn about healthy eating, how to exercise and the importance of cultivating good sleep habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Beyond that, primary school students have opportunities to be active in school through the Programme for Active Learning for those in Primary 1 and 2, and CCAs from Primary 3 onwards, as well as inter-class games, unstructured play during recess and school camps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Heat mitigation measures are also adopted to tackle rising temperatures and improve thermal comfort in schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Over the years, we have been careful not to rush into air-conditioning as the technology was not as energy efficient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Instead, we have relied on passive cooling solutions and we designed our schools for maximum natural ventilation and for classroom windows to be north-south facing to minimise heat transmission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: We are thus committed to ensuring that all students, regardless of which school they attend, have access to conducive learning environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: This includes exploring mixed mode cooling for classrooms as the science becomes clearer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: But like the trade-offs for mixed mode cooling, there are also trade-offs in our other suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Members, many of us in this House have spoken about students’ and teachers’ workload and stress, and we want our students to sleep more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: But we also want to double the number of PE hours, introduce entrepreneurship and inter-faith classes, and have white space Fridays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: At MOE, we are very protective of our students and teachers and are always looking to lower their workload and stress levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Let us instead take a leaf from Fuchun Primary's book and give our students the space to experience the joy of learning, growing and working together and not be in a rush to fill the curriculum with more and more things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: MOE will continue to study different ways of providing a conducive learning environment to our students, while actively managing all these trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: A common appreciation and love for arts and culture can also provide a common platform for Singaporeans to bond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students are exposed to Singapore’s artistic heritage, which helps them to understand our shared cultural story.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: When Amanda from Yew Tee Primary visited the National Gallery, she was introduced to Liu Kang's “Life By The River”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: She observed that “the people in the painting lived in wooden huts but today we live in HDB flats”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: In seeing how far we have come as a society, Amanda was not just looking at art, but she was connecting the dots across generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Live music performances by local performing arts groups are curated for lower secondary schools as part of their music education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students across different schools attend performances by local artists and appreciate local works at professional arts venue such as the Esplanade and the Victoria Concert Hall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Secondary 3 student Ghufayrah from Yishun Town Secondary School particularly enjoyed "Rasa Sayang" reimagined by the Singapore Chinese Orchestra.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: When students from different backgrounds share these cultural experiences together, they discover what unites us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: MOE schools serve as important shared spaces that provide a safe environment for students to learn respect and harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students can build positive relationships with one another, regardless of race or religion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Diana Pang suggested deepening interfaith education in schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, primary school students are introduced to the concept of dietary requirements, whether for health or religious reasons, by engaging in classroom activities such as planning a birthday party that is socially inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Students also participate in learning journeys to heritage sites, and celebrations of cultural festivals to develop respect and sensitivity to racial and religious issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: In doing so, MOE seeks to cultivate a deeper appreciation and understanding of Singapore’s multicultural and multi-religious society amongst our students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank all the Members once again for their very thoughtful suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Much of the discussion in this debate has been about AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: And in this AI age where algorithms shape choices and technology drives us into echo chambers that pull us apart, education is one of our most human acts of connection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: It teaches us empathy, critical thought, and our shared values that make us one united people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: Let us work together to shape an education system that will not just make our students smarter, but also more human and more connected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
text: A student-centric education system where we learn for life together, so we can nurture every Singaporean to achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Chair, since we launched SkillsFuture in 2015, our mission has been to provide Singaporeans with the opportunity to develop to their full potential throughout life, regardless of background.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a small, open economy, we continually invest in our people and empower them to grow skills, adapt to the changing work environment and seize new career opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Employers are also taking a more active role in upskilling their workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The training sector has matured in both breadth and scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We now have a range of training providers, from IHLs to specialist providers, offering diverse training across domains, closely guided by industry needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we look ahead, SkillsFuture must continue to evolve to better support Singaporeans in pursuing lifelong learning throughout their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With accelerating technological change and increasingly complex labour market demands, strengthening support for all Singaporeans has become even more critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Minister Desmond Lee has explained, the new agency will build on the strengths of both agencies: SSG's expertise in training and skills development, combined with WSG's employment facilitation ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This integration will enable us to connect skills development more closely with employment opportunities and career advancements, in line with the Economic Strategy Review’s recommendation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to support individual aspirations in upgrading, empower employers to take charge of their training needs, and develop a vibrant continuous education and training (CET) ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have empowered all Singaporeans to take charge of their own learning and upskilling journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The SkillsFuture Credit was one of our very first initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Every Singaporean aged 25 and above received an initial $500 credit for skills-related training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This supports adults to take that important first step in embracing lifelong learning, to improve their employment prospects or acquire new skills to pursue their interests and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over time, we have introduced new programmes to strengthen support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The SkillsFuture Level Up Programme (SFLP) was introduced in 2024 to support mid-career Singaporeans aged 40 and above to meaningfully upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many have been away from formal education for years and face competing priorities that make it challenging to take time off work for training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Without targeted support, they risk being left behind as their skills may become obsolete.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This year, we have also extended the Training Allowance to part-time training, with trainees receiving a fixed $300 monthly allowance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are encouraged by the response to the SFLP so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since its launch in May 2024, over 60,000 individuals have used their SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance has benefited over 5,000 individuals since it was first introduced in March 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will further enhance the SFLP to provide learners with more options to reskill and upskill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will expand the course catalogue to include Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) full qualification courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As part of a national skills credentialling system, such WSQ-accredited courses impart skills needed to perform various work tasks in line with industry manpower needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The inclusion of these courses ensures that SFLP learners can choose from a wider range of industry-relevant courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example would be the WSQ Specialist Diploma in Workplace Safety and Health offered by the National Trades Union Congress' LearningHub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This course trains participants in skills, such as safety and risk management and emergency response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Upon completion, participants can apply to become a registered Workplace Safety and Health Officer under the Workplace Safety and Health Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More details on the eligible WSQs will be released at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we continue to expand upskilling options, we also want to better support learners in navigating and making informed choices about their options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will take a key step by enhancing the digital experience for learners, to help them better navigate the various training offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, many Singaporeans are familiar with the MySkillsFuture portal, which they use to search for training courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SSG will revamp the MySkillsFuture portal, with two major improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SSG will launch a new course search experience that includes curated recommendations for in-demand skill areas, such as AI, occupation-based course exploration tools and an AI-powered chatbot for personalised guidance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One, the curated recommendations for in-demand skills areas – for those who know that they have a certain set of skills but are not entirely sure which occupation or career pathway to progress to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Two, the occupation-based course exploration tools – for those who know what career they are in, what trajectory they want, which in a particular industry, but want to know which skills or certifications to acquire for further progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Three, for those really not sure of which of these categories they fall in to or what they would like, we have a chatbot to be able to then understand their needs and to provide them with further guidance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SSG will also improve the course enrolment process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will make it easier for individuals to apply for courses immediately after having discovered them through the various search functions that I have just described and hence, reduce the administrative burden both on the individuals as potential learners and on training providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Overall, SSG's enhancements will make it easier for individuals to identify courses that are aligned with their career aspirations and reduce information asymmetry, as raised by Mr David Hoe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Hoe also suggested that training providers offer "taster" or trial overview lessons and that job shadowing and short learning journeys be introduced under SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some of our IHLs already provide information sessions for prospective learners to better understand the course content and objectives before signing up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For longer programmes, which require greater commitment, such as diplomas and degrees, learners can consider enrolling in stackable modules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This provides flexibility for learners to take the course without committing to the full programme upfront.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is also the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme where trainees benefit from career advisory and assistance in job searches and may undergo project work with companies, beyond classroom training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked how we are enhancing accessibility for persons with disabilities, so that they can better identify and take up courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SSG and SG Enable will continue to work with community partners to raise training providers' capabilities to deliver inclusive training, including in areas, like AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They conduct regular workshops on inclusive training methodologies and accommodations and have worked with the Institute for Adult Learning to develop courses for adult educators, so that they can better design and deliver inclusive training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SG Enable also provides a Capability Development Grant to help training providers who customise courses to meet the needs of persons with different disabilities and is working with SSG to explore ways to scale up the delivery of inclusive training by leveraging technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked how our polytechnics and ITE can support Singaporeans to pursue different lifelong learning pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, the polytechnics and ITE offer a range of pathways for lifelong learning, to meet the upskilling needs and career aspirations of different learners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes regularly reviewing course offerings and vacancies based on industry needs, employment outcomes and student interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Learners looking for more substantive upskilling or career switches can take up full qualifications, offered in both full-time and part-time modules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The IHLs have admissions pathways which recognise competencies gained in the workplace, instead of focusing narrowly on academic competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Learners who are looking for "just-in-time" upskilling can take up shorter modular micro-credentials, which offer bite-sized skills top-ups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We also recognise the important role that companies and employers play in skills development and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Employers are well-placed to know what skills are relevant, and guide workers' upskilling decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Both employers and workers can benefit when workers apply their newly acquired skills at the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the last decade, we have increased opportunities for employers to play a stronger role in the training of workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example is the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programme, which we launched in 2015, along with the broader SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The programme moved beyond classroom learning, to a model in which institutions and employers work together to help trainees learn in both the classroom and the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under this model, polytechnic and ITE students spend part of their time in structured learning environments and part of their time gaining hands-on experience in workplaces, earning a salary while they learn.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Employers play a crucial role as co-developers of the curriculum, ensuring that the skills taught directly address industry needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This success reflects the efforts of MOE and ITE and the commitment of more than 700 industry partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have been instrumental in teaching technical skills and providing tangible work experience for our trainees, allowing them to gain important life skills that they will carry with them throughout their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are glad that these employers see the value of the Work-Study Diploma programme in helping them develop their talent pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Around seven in 10 graduates continued with the employers who hired and trained them during the programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One such employer that exemplifies this commitment is STMicroelectronics, a semiconductor manufacturing company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: STMicroelectronics has worked closely with ITE to co-develop Work-Study programmes, together with other semiconductor industry partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The company has been expanding its Work-Study placements across programmes in exciting fields, including microelectronics, electronics and computer engineering and automation engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many graduates have chosen to build their careers with the company after completing their programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: An example is Nur'Iman, who joined STMicroelectronics as a technician on the Work-Study Diploma programme in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He was able to deepen his technical expertise through the programme, where he shadowed other technicians and engineers to build specialist knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In 2024, he was promoted to Assistant Maintenance Engineer, while also working on his final-year project, an AI computer vision solution for wafer defect detection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He graduated as the top student of his cohort in 2024 and continues to work for STMicroelectronics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are encouraged by the positive outcomes of the ITE Work-Study Diploma Programme and want to better recognise the efforts and commitment of our employer partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is in line with the Economic Strategy Review Committees' recommendations to support more flexible pathways that blend training and work to develop industry-relevant skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Hamid Razak also asked how we will strengthen the Work-Study Diploma pathway.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work with employers to provide meaningful training opportunities for ITE students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also simplify the process for disbursing these incentives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, the $15,000 incentive is paid out to companies as reimbursement upon the completion of specific qualifying activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Depending on the amount claimed and the activities completed, not all employers access the full $15,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The new $20,000 incentive will be fully disbursed at several milestones throughout the course duration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means an employer who sponsors an eligible trainee through the full Work-Study programme will receive the full amount.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will also make it easier for employers to claim these incentives by reducing the administrative processes required to access the funding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope that these enhancements will encourage more employers to come forward and build their talent pipelines, by offering meaningful training opportunities for our ITE graduates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to strengthen our support for companies, especially small and medium enterprises (SMEs), to identify their skills needs and access appropriate training for their employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, SSG introduced the SkillsFuture Queen Bee programme, where industry-leading companies provide skills advisory to SMEs in their networks, to help them identify and acquire skills needed to transform their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Grab is one such SkillsFuture Queen Bee and has provided short masterclasses to SMEs and their employees, on topics, like the Progressive Wage Model framework, and relevant skills training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These initiatives are useful in uplifting the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope more companies will come forward as SkillsFuture Queen Bees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SSG has also introduced digital workforce planning tools to support enterprises in workforce development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes TalentTrack, which employers can use to get insights on in-demand skills in their industries and identify suitable training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, SSG will create a comprehensive resource page of AI resources offered by SSG and its partners to make it easier for employers to identify resources for their AI transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Companies in all sectors will be able to access curated course recommendations to help them transform their business processes and to upskill their workers in AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These efforts will provide a good foundation that the new Statutory Board can build on to help companies, especially SMEs, continuously upskill their workforce to meet evolving industry demands and to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Lastly, we will continue to build a vibrant CET ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the last 10 years, our IHLs have become key players in the CET landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have significantly scaled up CET offerings and developed innovative upskilling pathways for adult learners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With the merger of SSG and WSG, MOE will continue to work with our IHLs to provide high-quality, industry-relevant and accessible training that leads to tangible career outcomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our IHLs are well-placed to deliver innovative and industry-relevant CET programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This places them at the nexus between education and research.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the IHLs can tap on these capabilities to translate frontier knowledge and new industry applications of technology into curricular.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IHLs also draw upon industry networks to ensure that both their faculty and their programmes remain updated on industry developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, it is common for IHL faculty to work directly with companies on industry projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Andre Low asked about how we would accredit high-quality micro-credentials such that they ensure tangible labour market value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Stackable micro-credentials are a key IHL innovation to improve accessibility in learning for adult workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Each micro-credential is a discrete unit of learning, with clear learning outcomes, assessment and certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Learners can earn academic credits which then stack to a CET full qualification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These micro-credentials can already be reflected on the Career and Skills Passport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example is the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SIT's competency-based CET degrees are delivered through stackable micro-credentials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SIT has engaged the industry to design each micro-credential around competencies and skillsets required for specific job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SIT continually collects feedback from learners and their employers, ensuring that the competencies can be applied directly at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Specifically on the recognition of micro-credentials across IHLs, we have piloted micro-credential pathways that are built upon courses from multiple IHLs, such as the Institution of Engineers Singapore's Chartered Engineer (Singapore) in Sustainability certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have done this in close partnership with industry partners, to ensure that these micro-credential pathways are industry-recognised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Andre Low also asked about overseas micro-credentials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Where there is a clear industry need, like in cloud software solutions, we have worked with employers, via the Singapore Computer Society, to recognise well-recognised overseas certifications for SkillsFuture support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In general, our focus would be to develop the local CET ecosystem to ensure rigorous quality assurance and alignment with Singapore's priorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Core to our effort in developing a vibrant CET ecosystem are our adult educators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Assoc Prof Terence Ho asked if we could do more to recognise excellence within the adult educator profession.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the last decade, we have embarked on a journey to professionalise the adult educator sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This equips adult educators with the core principles and skills for teaching adult learners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The TAEPP will also be tiered by levels, to better differentiate and recognise adult educators with more years of experience and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, more experienced and skilled adult educators can register as Professional or Senior Professional adult educators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will help to create meaningful progression for those looking to hone their skills and in turn enable training to be more effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are open to considering suggestions on how we can further recognise the work of exemplary adult educators and to showcase the important work they are doing to further uplift the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Choo Pei Ling spoke about ensuring that training leads to better outcomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For training to yield results, the training and workforce ecosystem must continue to work together to provide high-quality training, enable proactive employer involvement to steer training and recognise skills, and empower individuals to make thoughtful career and training choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since the start of our SkillsFuture journey in 2015, we have supported individual aspirations in upgrading, empowered employers to take charge of their training needs and developed a vibrant CET ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will share more about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Chair, we will continue to put Singaporeans at the centre of our efforts and ensure that no one is left behind in our journey towards a more skilled and resilient workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Chairman, AI is no longer a distant concept debated by experts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is already in our classrooms, in our workplaces and increasingly, in our homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In my Budget debate speech, I said that AI is not something that will arrive in a few years' time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is already reshaping how we learn, how we grow and how we work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And it forces us to confront a deeper question.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If AI can perform tasks that once required human cognition – writing, analysing, even coding – then what should humans focus on mastering?

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The rise of AI compels us to recalibrate not just our economy, but our understanding of human value.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: What should humans learn and grow in, when AI can do some of our work?

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: What do we find meaning in, when some of our time is freed up from work?

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: What do we want value and purpose to look like for ourselves and, better yet, for our children?

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In my speech, I will focus on the ways through which we are reshaping our education system, to prepare Singaporeans for a world transformed by AI: from our primary school to our pre-university students, to the graduates of our IHLs, to our workers on their lifelong journey of learning and upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must provide opportunities for everyone to learn how to harness AI to its full potential, at all points of their lifelong learning journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Darryl David spoke at length about the need for our education system to establish a strong foundation of skills in an AI-pervasive world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We want every student to learn about AI, to learn how to use AI, to learn with AI and, most importantly, to learn beyond AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They reflect four important ways to think about how we understand technology, use technology, collaborate with technology and transcend it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We are mindful that not all students come from homes with the same level of digital familiarity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: No student should be disadvantaged in this new era because of circumstance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Younger students will have lower exposure and closer supervision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They must build strong foundations and fundamentals in literacy, numeracy, reasoning as well as self-discipline to use AI wisely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We agree with Mr Alex Yam that students at a younger age should still learn their core foundational knowledge and skills and not use AI as a shortcut to their learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Yam also asked how AI literacy is being strengthened for our students, while ensuring that we address ethics, academic integrity, bias and over-reliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When we say students will learn about AI, they may learn in their Cyber Wellness classes how to identify deepfakes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Not just as a technical skill, but as a defence against misinformation in a world where not everything we see or hear is real.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When we say students will learn to use AI, they will use AI tools in the updated "Code for Fun" programme that the Minister of State Rahayu had mentioned, and in subjects, like design and technology, or general paper, to generate ideas, refine arguments or compare sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But they will also be guided to evaluate what the AI produces, check its accuracy and include their personal voice and opinions instead of just accepting what AI generates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When we say students will learn with AI, they may use AI as a learning partner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Using AI tools, like the Learning Assistant in the Singapore Student Learning Space, they can develop multiple perspectives about an issue through discussion with Learning Assistant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: This will prompt them to think deeper about their views and suggests alternative perspectives that they may have failed to consider.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And when we say students will learn beyond AI, it means they engage in real-world problem solving, developing human qualities, like empathy and 21st Century Competencies, like inventive thinking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For example, in Applied Learning Programmes, students may be asked to consider ways to reduce food waste in schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They can use AI to generate multiple suggestions within seconds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But students will need to evaluate feasibility of these solutions, for example, cost, resourcing and their peers' preferences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: This includes retaining the emphasis on in-person assessments making greater use of oral explanations and the demonstration of process, not just final output when it comes to assessments where AI tools can be used.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Technology will evolve, but integrity must remain non-negotiable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will work closely with relevant agencies to ensure responsible adoption aligned with national AI governance principles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: AI is already performing tasks we once thought required uniquely human cognition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And while we can guide students' exposure within the schools, we cannot control what they encounter outside of schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: So, the real question is not how students use AI, it is who they become in an age shaped by AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: This is why the most important "Learn", is for our students to learn beyond AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If AI can generate answers in seconds, then our students must learn how to ask better questions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If AI can process vast amounts of data, then our students must develop judgement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And if AI can imitate language, then our students must cultivate character.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: There is no better time than now to reflect on what gives humans value.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The ability to choose what is right, not just what is efficient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Perhaps it lies in our compassion, the ability to connect, to comfort and to inspire.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Perhaps it lies in our courage, the courage to shape a better future, even if it requires more effort than in the present.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But whatever it is, we have to recognize and build on these values with urgency so that what makes us human will continue to be what is most valued in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our education system cannot simply train our children to chase the latest AI qualification.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It must equip them to interpret the world critically, empathise deeply and build lives of meaning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Ng Chee Meng asked how our IHLs can better design curriculum to ensure our graduates remain employable in an AI-transformed future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Today, full-time undergraduates in our universities and students in our polytechnics and ITE already learn about AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But in this new era, exposure alone is not enough.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: This is done through partnerships with industries, sector-specific task forces, curriculum advisory committees and direct feedback from employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But just as in our schools, IHL students cannot stop at learning about AI, using AI or even collaborating with AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They must also learn beyond AI to sharpen what makes them distinctly human in an age of intelligent machines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Because in the future, it will not be enough to know how to deploy AI tools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Graduates must be able to define problems clearly, work across disciplines and persuade others to act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We also ensure that students apply what they learn in real-world challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: At the recent Manus AI for All Hackathon, I witnessed how students worked alongside SMEs and freelancers to solve actual business problems in just a few hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Others built AI-powered marketing assistants for small food and beverage businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: One team developed a platform for a debate coach to help competitive debaters practise live argumentation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These were real clients, real constraints and real stakes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These experiences will help our graduates translate knowledge into economic value.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But more importantly, they will help students discover their human value before they even enter the workforce, in their ability to frame problems, exercise judgement under uncertainty, recover from failure and persuade fellow humans to try something new.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: (In Mandarin):   With the rapid pace of technological advancement, it is more important than ever for our education system to prepare our students for a world transformed by AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We want every student to learn about AI, learn to use AI, learn with AI and, most importantly, learn beyond AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They reflect four important ways to think about how we understand technology, use it, collaborate with it and transcend it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: AI is already performing tasks we once thought required uniquely human cognition – analysing data, drafting reports and even writing code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And while we can guide students' exposure within school, we cannot control what they encounter outside of it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: So, the real question is not how students use AI; it is who they become in an age shaped by AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Hence, beyond technical skills that will help them create economic value, it is even more critical for students to discern their human value in this new era.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Ultimately, no matter how quickly technology evolves, it is our human skills and cherished values, such as empathy, resilience and hard work, which will stand the test of time and serve the next generation well in a turbulent world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Rather than just teaching students how to use AI, we are nurturing individuals with the competencies and will to act for the good of society from primary school to our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Before graduating, we will ensure that students have opportunities to gain real-world exposure and understand their human value proposition as they enter the workforce. : As Ms Lee Hui Ying pointed out, our educators have an important role to play to help our students prepare for the AI-enabled world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our educators are modelling how to think, question and act responsibly in an AI-enabled world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We recognise that this transition will require adjustment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will phase the changes thoughtfully, provide clear guidelines and ensure that our educators are supported as they adapt their pedagogy in an AI-enabled environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Educators can also tap on centrally provisioned AI tools through the Singapore Student Learning Space, as well as tools that streamline administrative tasks and free up time to focus on what matters most, which is their students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Ultimately, AI should empower our educators to focus on the deeply human aspects of education – guidance, mentorship and connection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: No algorithm can replace the instinct of an educator who senses when a student is discouraged or is facing family challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: No algorithm can replace an educator who inspires her students to rise above their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The same applies to our educators in our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As Assoc Prof Terence Ho mentioned, they too must be equipped to guide students in navigating AI not just as an educational tool, but as a transformative force across industries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our IHLs are deepening staff capabilities in adopting AI for both teaching and assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Existing educators are also provided with training and support to build confidence and proficiency in using AI responsibly and effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our IHLs are also deploying AI tools that enhance learning and assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These tools augment classroom learning and help educators monitor student progress and customise their interventions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Meanwhile, the National University of Singapore has a tool called ScholAIstic that enables educators to design structured AI interactions where students can practice real-world conversations in a safe environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: This works for social work client interviews and courtroom cross-examinations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Republic Polytechnic's Diploma in Pharmaceutical Science also incorporates the use of an AI-based simulation platform for students to practice clinical skills in safe, customisable medical care scenarios.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Assoc Prof Ho also asked how we can facilitate sharing across IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our institutions have established platforms for educators to exchange best practices in tech-enabled teaching through communities of practice, staff-led forums and conferences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For example, the biennial National Technology-Enhanced Learning Conference brings educators together to explore emerging trends in educational technology and AI, and to translate these into better learning outcomes for students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As AI continues to evolve, our schools and IHLs will continue to evolve with it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will update not only what we teach, but how we teach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will work closely with students, educators and industry partners so that our graduates are prepared not just for today's jobs, but for tomorrow's uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But AI education does not end at graduation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As the Prime Minister noted in his Budget speech, our workers will also need new skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil spoke about supporting SMEs in upskilling their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Beyond that, we must also empower individual workers to take ownership of their own learning journeys.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In an AI-transformed world, lifelong learning is no longer optional.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In the coming years, AI literacy will not be a specialised skill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It will be as fundamental as digital literacy is today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Every worker, regardless of sector or job role, should understand what AI can and cannot do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Workers must develop fluency, which is the ability to apply AI meaningfully within their own domain, solve real problems and create value in their organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how MOE is working with our partners to expand accessible and practical AI upskilling pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: First, we will help individuals understand their current level of AI readiness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: SSG has partnered the Singapore Institute of Technology to develop a simple self-diagnostic tool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Second, we will make it easier for individuals to navigate the wide range of AI-related training options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These range from full qualifications for career transitions, to shorter modules for skills upgrading within existing roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: There are full time courses, or shorter courses for those looking for a skills-top up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Choice is good, but it can sometimes be overwhelming.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: To address this, SSG will better curate and signpost high-quality courses, tagging them according to AI worker archetypes and highlighting those with strong training outcomes and employer support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will also monitor take-up rates, completion outcomes, and work relevance of such courses, to ensure that these programmes translate into real skills and real opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Upskilling must lead to tangible progress for our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We hope alumni will use these opportunities not only to deepen their skills, but to reconnect with their institutions and their professional networks, reinforcing a culture of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Through all of these moves, we are equipping our workers with the tools to adapt in an AI-transformed landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But beyond mastering AI as a tool, we must not lose sight of the qualities that set us apart.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As AI becomes more powerful, these capabilities will become more valuable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Chairman, we are living through a period of rapid change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is understandable that some may feel uncertain or anxious, about what lies ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our schools and Institutes of Higher Learning stand ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If AI can optimise systems, our people must uphold values.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If AI can accelerate progress, our people must decide its direction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Chairman, what do we mean when we say we want to “Learn for Life Together”?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Meaningful and effective learning requires an active connection with others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It comes alive through dialogue, through inquiry and through social engagement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Whether in the classroom or beyond its walls, reciprocal learning occurs between learners together: the child and parent, the student and teacher, or even between students and colleagues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Learning can occur in school, in our homes, on the field, in the marketplace or in our community hubs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Success in education, therefore, best emerges from strong partnerships between schools, parents, and the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Today, I will share about how we are deepening this commitment through enhanced support for our Mother Tongue languages, expanded provisions for students with SEN, and stronger foundations for students’ social and emotional well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have come a long way since the introduction of our bilingual policy in our early years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The rest could read in only one language or not at all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The English language has facilitated inter-ethnic communication, social cohesion and participation in the global economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Simultaneously, our Mother Tongue languages (MTLs) anchor us to our cultural heritage, history and values, while allowing Singaporeans to gain a competitive edge internationally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In nurturing our students' Mother Tongue proficiency, we know that there is no one-size-fits-all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For stronger students, Higher Mother Tongue and the Language Elective Programmes allow deeper engagement with language, literature and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For other students who may need more time to develop their proficiency with the language, they are supported via the Mother Tongue Support Programme and Foundation Mother Tongue in primary school, and G1 and G2 Mother Tongue in secondary school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These are key features of our Mother Tongue curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: However, as Ms Lee Hui Ying notes, strengthening Mother Tongue learning requires continual refinement to enable every student to learn their MTL to as high a level as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: At the primary level, we have introduced more varied learning approaches, such as the MTL SOAR programme to cultivate MTL reading from young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: At the secondary level, we have reviewed the higher MTL eligibility criteria to expand access to our MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Importantly, as Dr Hamid Razak noted, language learning does not end in the classroom.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Languages must be allowed to come alive through speech, through practice, and using them actively to communicate with others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To learn and to use our MTLs for life together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Since 2005, we established the Mother Tongue Languages Learning and Promotion Committees (MTLLPCs) to help our students experience their MTLs as living languages through partnerships with the community and by exploring creative and innovative ways of learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For example, many students might find it difficult to remember and recite a five-minute long passage in their Mother Tongues, but when stitched into a tune or a song, it becomes easier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mila Eliza, from Opera Estate Primary School, was one of the participants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mila had always been a soft-spoken student, particularly in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In class, she would often answer her Cikgu's questions hesitantly in English.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: But through Katapella, Mila grew into her voice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Rehearsal by rehearsal, the habit of projecting and speaking up in Malay grew increasingly natural for her.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These days, when her cikgu asks her questions, she is more confident of answering loudly and clearly in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Experiences like Katapella bring language learning to life and give students a chance to explore the beauty of their MTL and build confidence in its use.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The increased funding will support a wider range of activities and programmes for students and parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These include songwriting, radio broadcasting, debate and digital content creation, all in our students’ Mother Tongue languages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In this coming tranche, we are keen to also give particular attention to supporting parents in their children’s early childhood years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As the Tamil saying goes, “ஐந்தில் வளையாதது ஐம்பதில் வளையுமா?”, or “If it doesn't bend at five, will it bend at 50?” The early childhood years are critical for language development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We hope that consistent exposure in these years will create a strong foundation and appreciation of MTL.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Many young parents are hesitant to speak to their children in their Mother Tongues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They say: “I’m not good at it myself, what if I teach them the wrong thing?” As we tell our children, just try.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Learning an MTL is not necessarily about perfection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It is about sharing, in its first-hand language, our stories, our roots, our heritage, and our culture with our children and the next generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In the spirit of trying, recently, I learnt a Chinese saying, "一寸光阴, 一寸金,寸金难买寸光阴".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Some of you might remember your parents or teachers reciting this to you as a child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It is a beautiful way to inculcate values – that an inch of time is worth an inch of gold and we cannot buy time even with gold.
