speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It is a poignant reminder that time is precious and indeed, our MTLs have a special ability to bring out the true depth and value of such messages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I encourage parents of young children to sign up and take these baby steps towards learning for life, alongside their children, with us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It is also an opportunity for them to build close and nurturing relationships with their young children at an early age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Bilingualism is a cornerstone of our education system and indeed, our Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: With differentiated support in schools and further grounding in the community, we intend to strengthen MTLs as a vibrant anchor of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Another area where close partnership of school and community support is important is in our support for students with SEN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Prof Kenneth Poon asked about how support for such students considers their varied access to external resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For each of these students, schools provide support based on their specific learning needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Schools provide a range of interventions for learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For example, the TRANSIT programme, which stands for TRANsition Support for InTegration for Primary 1 students, focuses on behaviour management, while the School-based Dyslexia Remediation Programme supports students’ literacy skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Where students require medical or therapy support unavailable in MOE or our schools, our schools will then facilitate referrals to external resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As we continue to strengthen our school-based provisions, we will be able to support every student with mild SEN in mainstream schools, regardless of background.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For students with moderate-to-severe SEN however, we support them in SPED schools, with specialised support and customised teaching and learning approaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As Ms Denise Phua shared, demand for SPED schools has risen in recent years, driven by an increasing number of students diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder with Intellectual Disability (ASD-ID).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: First, we will partner MINDS to establish additional campuses for the three MINDS schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These will operate from interim sites in the East and Central regions progressively from the second half of 2026.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Second, we will relocate MINDS Woodlands Gardens School to a larger interim site with increased capacity in the North region from 2027.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Third, we will partner three SSAs – APSN Education Services Ltd, Autism Association (Singapore) and St Andrew's Mission Hospital – to set up three new schools across the island.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: One of the schools, run by APSN Education Services Ltd, will operate from the second half of 2026 at an interim site in the North-East region and we will share more details soon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These new and expanded schools will allow us to serve more children with ASD-ID, while also benefiting some existing MINDS students by shortening their daily school commutes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: There are also other ongoing efforts to set up permanent sites for existing SPED schools that cater to various disability types, including the Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore School (West), Grace Orchard School and Maitri School.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Through this expansion, we seek to deepen our commitment to supporting every child in learning for life together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In doing so, we will ensure that every child has a community where they belong, where their needs are supported and where they can grow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We are conscious that programmes and spaces cannot be effective without dedicated educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As Dr Charlene Chen has noted, support for educators ensures sustainable outcomes for our students with SEN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In mainstream schools, we adopt a tiered approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: All educators have a baseline understanding of inclusive classroom practices, so that students with SEN can learn alongside their peers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: On top of this, teachers trained in special needs and SEN Officers provide deeper expertise and support other colleagues to nurture an inclusive education landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To ensure adequate support capacity, we review schools' resourcing needs regularly and adjust provisions accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For example, all primary schools have a minimum of two SEN Officers, while those with higher and more complex needs may have up to four SEN Officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will continue to work with our schools to build up this capability and capacity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In SPED schools, structured training allows our educators to develop deep expertise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: From 2025, we have enhanced access to baseline training by increasing the number of places for NIE's Diploma in Special Education, from 150 to 180 per year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: MOE has also been working with SSAs and SPED schools to deepen disability knowledge through Communities of Practice on specific disability profiles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Platforms like Communities of Practice allow SPED educators to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams to meet students' complex learning needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Over the next decade, we recognise that recruitment and retention of SPED educators will be critical to support the sector's expansion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This followed earlier efforts to strengthen professionalism by introducing career tracks, roles profiles and competency frameworks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: With the strong support of the SSAs, SPED schools have since adopted the recommended salary ranges and made progress to implement stronger performance-based remuneration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have also introduced the SPED Leadership Development Programme to nurture SPED educator leaders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will continue to coordinate sector-level recruitment efforts and work with SSAs to develop SPED into a promising and viable career option.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Our schools and teachers certainly cannot do this work alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Our communities, our families and our homes are anchors for many aspects of our lives and their significance is particularly salient for our students with SEN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Home is where our students apply their learning from school to everyday life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In our primary schools, parents of children with dyslexia can read aloud daily with their children to reinforce literacy skills at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Likewise, in delivering the National SPED curriculum, teachers emphasise family involvement to help students practise and use daily living skills taught in SPED schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We agree with Ms Denise Phua that, for students with SEN to flourish, it takes a village.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We must work closely and sustainably for the long term, with families and community partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In General Education schools, MOE's national advisory council, COMmunity and Parents in Support of Schools (COMPASS) comprises stakeholders, such as parents, industry and self-help groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: COMPASS has initiated different efforts for parents and community partners to cultivate meaningful school-home partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: One such COMPASS initiative is the set-up of the Parents-for-Parents (P4P) network, to deepen support for parents of children with SEN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Based on their own experiences, COMPASS members recognised a need for peer support to better navigate the challenges of supporting children with special educational needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The P4P network was started to address this gap.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: P4P connects parents of children with SEN with each other, to provide valuable peer support when navigating uncertainty, key decisions and transitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: P4P also extends school and system-level support when needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This is an example of how organic, parent-driven support can scale effectively for the benefit of our schools and our students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This commitment to partnership extends to our SPED schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These schools will develop a deeper understanding of parents' perspectives and needs to provide more focused support for parents with children of higher needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Partnerships between our schools, parents and the community make a real difference in our students' lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: While undergoing baking training at Metta School, Rachel Tan learnt that the path to the right career is paved with detours and self-discovery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Through an internship arranged by Metta School and industry partners, Rachel realised, despite her technical skills, the day-to-day of the baking industry was not ideal for her.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To figure out her next steps, Metta School, Rachel, and her family leaned into her natural strengths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Today, with her keen eye for detail and gift for genuine connection, Rachel thrives as a Housekeeping Officer at Changi Airport where she brightens many a traveller's stressful day.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In 2025, Rachel won the Changi Service G.E.M Programme for her exceptional service.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Rachel's success demonstrates the power of strong partnerships between schools and families to help our students reach their potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To enable such partnerships, we are extending MOE's digital solutions to SPED schools to make communication more seamless.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This will also reduce the administrative burden, freeing up teachers' time for teaching and improve student outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These partnerships in schools are just the beginning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Recognising that our students require support beyond the schooling years, we are committed, as a government, to supporting our students along this journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I look forward to sharing our recommendations when ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Across these areas, we see that meaningful educational outcomes require a community of support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Dr Charlene Chen asked about our support for our students' well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Our children develop resilience and socio-emotional well-being in community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Through the CCE curriculum, MOE equips students with developmentally appropriate skills for emotional regulation, peer support and help-seeking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Beyond the classroom, each school's ecosystem of support includes proactive monitoring, trained peer support leaders and access to school counsellors and community mental health resources when needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Over the years, we have also explored innovative methods to support our students' well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Like Ms Elysa Chen, MOE recognises the potential of the arts in this area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: International research indicates that sustained emphasis in arts education is more effective than one-off activities for students' well-being and social-emotional development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: All our students learn music and art for eight years taught by specialised teachers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The activities and tasks are designed for students to learn social-emotional competencies at the same time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: All our lower secondary school students learn English Literature where they explore emotions, human interactions and identities through different genres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Schools too can customise their own programmes and curate student-led activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Where there are effective best practices, school leaders have platforms to share these practices with other schools, so that students can benefit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: At its core, MOE recognises that the work of supporting our children takes many hands coming together and never alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Indeed, we can all learn for life together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Malay. :   Bilingualism is a cornerstone of our education system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mother Tongue Language learning transcends the classroom – because languages come alive when they are regularly spoken and shared with others and developed together within the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In this spirit, we established the Mother Tongue Languages Learning and Promotion Committees in 2005 to help students develop an interest in and deepen understanding of their Mother Tongue through collaboration with community partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The increased funding will support a wider range of activities and programmes for students and parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These include supporting creative approaches in Mother Tongue, including songwriting, radio broadcasting, debate and digital content creation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will pay particular attention to supporting parents during their child’s early years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As the Malay saying goes, “Bend the bamboo when it is still a shoot”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The early childhood years are critical for language development and consistent exposure will create a strong foundation for Mother Tongue appreciation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Many young parents may be hesitant and lack the confidence to talk to their children in Mother Tongue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Just as we tell our students in school, we encourage parents to be confident and try speaking Mother Tongue at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Learning a language is not necessarily about achieving perfection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: On the contrary, see it as an opportunity to share stories that convey values, heritage and culture to our children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I encourage parents with young children to take advantage of these measures to further reinforce the use of Mother Tongue in the home and family environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Like planting seeds that bear fruit, the outcomes of changes to the education system will take time and should be viewed from a long-term perspective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In fact, we are increasingly seeing success and progress in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To Mr Abdul Muhaimin’s query, I am pleased to share that the Malay community has shown good progress and performance in educational achievement over the years, with higher percentages obtaining post-secondary and university qualifications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We work together with relevant agencies and community partners to ensure that no student is denied the opportunity to pursue higher education due to financial difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: For example, Yayasan MENDAKI offers the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy as well as other financial assistance schemes, study loans and scholarships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We will continue to strengthen this partnership with schools, teachers and community partners to ensure that our students continue to thrive regardless of their background. : Allow me to conclude by sharing another saying, “Berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We share the heavy burdens and carry the light loads together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Whether we are taking small steps to speak in our MTLs to our children, forging close partnerships to support our students with SEN, or strengthening the well-being of our students, MOE recognises that we are not, and cannot be, alone on this shared educational journey to mould the future of our nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: By learning for life together, we will build a Singapore where every child can reach their fullest potential, and where our rich tapestry of languages and abilities continues to be a source of collective strength for our society and generations to come.

speaker: The Chairman
text: There are 25 of you who have filed cuts.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will prioritise those who have filed longer cuts first.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I suggested in my cut, Minister, about the possibility of using AI to create avatar teachers to to minimise or to positively impact the teacher-student ratio.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the Minister share if MOE is willing to consider this?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, even as we create a better teacher-student ratio, I would like to also go to my second clarification, which is to ensure that the direction we have taken towards reducing class sizes continues, not so much for an absolute number, Minister, but perhaps for the appropriate class size to suit the needs of the students that are taking that particular subject.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And the third clarification, Sir, is regarding the centre-based advanced learning modules for students in primary schools, I would like to ask Minister if MOE is prepared to consider extending this programme into the secondary school sector, perhaps to cater to some of those students who are a little bit of late bloomers, so that they also have opportunities and options for this programme in secondary school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Already in the Student Learning Space, which is used not just at home, but also in the classroom to accompany teaching and pedagogy, students already have recourse to online material, as well as the use of AI tools, for example, the learning feedback assistant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we will continue to look at the ways as technology improves to leverage it, in order to augment teaching and learning.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is the direction we are heading.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as I said earlier, there are non-trivial considerations and we have to study this very carefully.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we have a school-based programme and a centre-based advanced module.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In secondary schools, there are already schools, including some of the Integrated Programme schools, and in fact, all secondary schools have programmes as well as experienced teachers to help to stretch students who are more inquisitive, have talents in certain domains.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But at the MOE level we also have MOE electives and programmes to empower some of these students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the school level and national level, we have Olympiad for maths and science.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These also allow some of these students to be stretched as well.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The first is regarding on supporting students from disadvantaged background.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Second, what proportion of this 50,000 represent the total number of disadvantaged students?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And third, more broadly, while more additional resources are given to supporting students from disadvantaged background, I also understand that not all schools start from the same baseline.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Some have a stronger alumni network that they can tap on or community resources.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I wonder whether would MOE ensure a stronger baseline across all schools so that students from disadvantaged background, regardless of which school they are in, will have equitable access to opportunities.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I understand that students can take public transport to GEP centres.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: However, if the younger students are in Primary 3, about nine years old, do we have a guideline in terms of the reasonable commute time?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: MOE also earlier shared about the challenges on teachers recruitment about, including competition between private and public sectors.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I wonder whether MOE has thought about the occupational mobility as a factor.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Because I have heard from many who say that if you join teaching, you cannot really see a career switch.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: So, I wonder, can MOE share its perspective on this narrative and perhaps, more importantly, assure prospective teachers that teaching also equips them with transferable skills that allows them to be valuable across different sectors?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, the Opportunity Fund, whether students know about it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our schools have data of the students who are more disadvantaged and who may need more support, whether they are from a lower SES family or because they face more complex challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This information is shared with students as well as parents, but certainly we will see what more we can do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each school will have a sense of the students that will benefit from the Opportunity Fund, and encourage them and work through the barriers to enable them to benefit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those are centres which run the centre-based advanced modules.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we allow schools to decide for themselves how best to enable their students to access these centre-based advanced modules.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member also asked a question about recruitment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have not been able to follow that train, Mr Chairman.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: The earlier question is one on students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: I wonder whether there will be a stronger baseline baseline for support for all schools.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: Because for some schools they do have resources in terms of alumni networks and community resources.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: So, would we be able to consider a stronger baseline so that every child, regardless of which school they are at, if they come from a disadvantaged background, they have access to equitable resources.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: One of the feedback that is often heard is that if you join teaching, you cannot really move to other sectors.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: I wonder what MOE's view is on this narrative, and whether for prospective teachers that are coming in, maybe it is about highlighting the different skillsets that they have that allows them to be able to move between sectors as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the stronger baseline of support, we provide the schools with resources from HQ.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Schools also have the school advisory committees, where not just alumni, but also very well-meaning individuals who join the school advisory committees contribute resources, but also contribute networks for the schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But certainly, through ComLink+, as I mentioned earlier, integrating more intensively with our schools, with our school student welfare officers, with our school leaders, we want to provide not just resources, but a network of SSAs and resources to empower the schools to help these children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because the problems are not always with the children in school, but sometimes, in their families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The role of a teacher is multi-faceted and complex.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They come up with projects to improve school operations and teaching.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, they pick up lots of skills which are valuable in of its own right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also send our teachers for teacher work attachments so that they can see what is happening in other sectors – not just to benefit teaching, but also to give them a sense of the kinds of skillsets that are out there that are needed in industry broadly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
text: The first is regarding the four "Learns" for AI.

speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is that while I note the Minister of State mentioned the role of performing arts and literature, does the Ministry see an even larger role for the humanities to foster critical thinking and ethical judgement in the AI age?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: So, yes, the four "Learns", the guidelines have been put out across Singapore to all schools and teachers will be able to access them.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: On the second question on subjects, I think AI should and can be used across many, many different subjects and we will strive to work towards a system where teachers, regardless of the subjects they teach, are able to think about how AI can be best used.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number one is on the DSA arms race.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We know that applications are surging and I hear that there is a lot more interest in this space as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, how does the MOE intend to reduce the preparation advantage, increase more authentic school-based nominations and reduce all this portfolio-gaming?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second one is on yet another arms race.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I did not raise it in my speech, but it is about the internship arms race.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know of some residents, they are from slightly disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They shared with me that when it comes to internships, they have very little connections and networks, and they lose out to some of their classmates who sometimes have four or five options, and even have internships stacked upon one another.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How do we address that so that they get more equal access?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The third one is on the PSLE pilot through-train.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I heard that the Minister said that he will consider.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I was just wondering, is this kind of a "yes", "no" or "maybe" response, because this has been spoken about for quite a long time?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And the last one is on SPED schools for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Physical capacity is definitely needed, but I think very importantly, and I volunteer in special schools, so, a lot of the constraints is not in the physical capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I want to ask MOE on what it will do in the manpower space so that it is not just business as usual.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can we tap on, for example, specialist manpower to address this gap.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number two is, I think the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has mentioned that there is a review of salaries of educators and teacher aids.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But the SPED schools are run by a lot of the other professionals as well such as occupational therapists, speech pathologists, psychologists, coaches and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And I ask for MOE, as it always looks at SPED educators, to also focus on this other very important group; because retention is capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And the last one is on making sure that the poaching from SPED mainstream schools and sometimes MOE, the Ministry of Health does not recur.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Phua, you might want to get to your last clarification.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And how do we intend to grow the pie to address this manpower challenge?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Chairman, I will just address the first one on DSA.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The DSA was really introduced to make sure that we offer our students more pathways.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Those with different talents to have the pathway to get into the school that they want, and we are able to develop the potential for the interest that they have.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And I think it is something we acknowledge, it can always constantly be improved in terms of the selection process, how we identify potential to make sure it does not escalate into an arms race.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: We have done quite a number of significant efforts in the past couple years.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: For example, in the Sports School now, you have multi-sport athletes and selection is based on their displayed potential to specialise subsequently in one particular sport.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And then, that helps to take away that desire to overprepare and then the desire to escalate it into an arms race.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: It really is the case that beyond increasing the capacity, she is right that the attending challenges must be addressed with regard to manpower.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: In light of that, the work has already started.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: On top of that, I hear the Member's concern about how it can be quite challenging to tap on the same pool with regard to manpower, and the concern is that if you go into the SPED teaching industry, does it mean it is an opportunity cost for teachers or psychologists, vice versa?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And that is something that, in terms of hiring, we are doing quite a fair bit, including organising the SPED teachers career fair, as well as working with SPED schools to have representation in the career fair of our autonomous universities as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, we are working hard at it and we are also having engagements with the SSAs to see where the challenges are in terms of hiring, as well as retention of manpower.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Those who come into the SPED industry are really those who care for the children and care for the needs of the SPED students, and that is something that we want to be able to retain, as part of the wider fraternity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Chairman, I will deal with the other two questions that Ms Denise Phua raised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sometimes, the children push themselves without realising that they are putting themselves through undue stress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But aspiration and motivation on the one side, and stress and pressure on the other side are two faces of a coin.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the internship arms race came about when we speak to IHLs, we speak to companies, we speak to students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Not just IHL students, by the way, even your upper secondary school students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a reflection of how some employers are saying, "Well, your students who apply, applicants are all so good, the results are all great, almost all similar.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I distinguish by looking at their character, their leadership, their empathy, whether they are toxic or whether they are empathetic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we think an internship will allow us to get a feel of them", and there, you create a certain pathway.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, taken to extremes, motivation and drive can become unhealthy not just for the individual and the family, but for society as a whole.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And when we fine tune and calibrate or reform a system, we have to be mindful that it is not just one exam or the exam itself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It could be what the exam results are being used for, whether it is a PSLE result, A-level exam results and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, this is a very large system issue that we need to tackle carefully and thoughtfully.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will not be closed off to any idea.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But every idea, including what I mentioned in the speech, comes with its tensions and trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for every idea raised, there will be people in opposition to that idea.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, through-train, then who will through-train to some of the more popular secondary schools?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Will it cause the race to be brought down from PSLE to before Primary 1 admission?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All these are considerations, but we will start this conversation with a very broad open mind.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Chairman, I acknowledge that many initiatives already exist.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Does MOE set benchmarks to ensure fidelity and consistency of implementation across schools?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Otherwise, how does the Ministry detect when resilience building is weaker in certain schools?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry assure this House that students' access to structured resilience education, timely counsellor support, for example, does not vary meaningfully from school to school?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: My second question on special needs and behavioural issues among students in mainstream schools.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Could the Ministry share whether it tracks how long it takes on average from first observation to deployment of additional support in Primary 1?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And whether the Ministry has studied whether incorporating a short structured executive function baseline into the existing Primary 1 framework could shorten the window and enable earlier manpower calibration at the cohort level, especially when support density is higher in certain classes?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: As to the level of access in terms of the variety, I do not have the number at this point of time to answer the Member's question.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: They do have an acute awareness of some of the conditions or the difficulty that students may have.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And at a moment's notice, if let us say they find that a child is struggling, for which it may invite additional resource, say, for example, our teachers trained in special needs, or even our SEN officers, this can be given within the organic school resource.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Beyond which, as we have already mentioned, in terms of any specific interventions under transit, in terms of the students in Primary 1 specifically, transitioning into Primary 1, as well as the school-based dyslexia remediation, these are available as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The question on SEN, that in terms of the timeline, if I understood the question?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, with regard to the identification and deployment of resources, with regard to the timeline from which it is first identified to the time where it is being intervened, I will invite the Member to also ask another Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And whether we track it as well, we do track it, but I will just have to defer to a Parliamentary Question so that we can answer and give a considered response for the Member.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Chair, let me start by thanking Minister Desmond Lee for his explanation about challenges in the modern classroom, including this very challenging question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My issue here is just that why is it only five marks?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I appreciate that CCAs are an integral part of a student's educational journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As someone who has taken part in three CCAs in my time in secondary school, including one which we shared, I could not agree more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That said, my point is that there is a clear opportunity cost when already overburdened teachers are asked to take on yet more duties, and as explained in my cut, to the detriment of teaching functions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This then robs our students of more teacher attention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, in this context, my questions are twofold.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Does the Minister agree that even in the age of AI, sustaining human instruction in our classrooms, especially in primary, but also SPED schools, remains paramount?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We have received substantial ground feedback that staff turnover has led to teaching assistants being tasked with covering for some of these departures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If so, my second question is whether the Ministry will consider that even as it faces the very real constraints that Minister Lee shared about ramping up the teaching core quickly, will they expand Allied Educators specifically in Teaching and Learning as an interim stop-gap measure?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The answer to the first part of the question I responded by Parliamentary Question the last time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The answer is yes, more details in the Hansard.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: First, for the vulnerable students, was wondering if the Minister could elaborate on how collaboration between schools and SSAs will be structured to assist students with higher needs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: For example, is there a formal framework that encourages and incentivises partnership between these different agencies?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Second question is on the DSA, just following up on Acting Minister's response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Competition can be constructive if it supports both individual development and the long-term talent pipeline, I think the issue here is early specialising, which distorts the talent market in favour of those with resources rather than those with talent and potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, are there plans for MOE to collaborate more closely with relevant domain experts and agencies in the area of sports?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: For example, it could be with the High Performance Sport Institute and the national sports associations, to develop clearer national criteria or progression frameworks for early talent identification in sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This could be an adoption of some of the criteria that the Sports School already uses and to apply that for other schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: My third question is on the demand for Primary 1 places.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I was wondering if MOE has studied the feasibility of expanding the footprint or intake of highly sought after primary schools to ease concentrated demand?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State had mentioned that the IHLs are the nexus between education and research, and I agree.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: However, in practice, the teaching communities, including the adjunct and external faculty and the research communities, they often operate in parallel.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a structured approach to better integrate academic research, industry expertise and the delivery of lifelong learning?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Are there plans to review the incentive structures to better support faculty in such integration?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will deal with the question on working with agencies, SSAs and Primary 1 places.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Senior Minister of State Janil with CET; and then Senior Minister of State David on DSA and early specialisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But ComLink is the national flagship to build relationships between schools and our SSAs and partners to better support our students from the perspective of the schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are various ideas that have been raised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, some have suggested expanding the places for certain schools where they are very popular and hope to then have more diversity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The downside is, of course, that it may cause other schools to hollow out and you know that schools have had to merge over the years and with falling cohort sizes and with more mergers, if we were to do as the Member had suggested, there is a risk that there will be even more mergers, affecting accessibility in terms of proximity for families.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In truth, the autonomous universities and the IHLs need to look at the issue of how they integrate practice, research, education and other pastoral duties, for example, as fit for their student population, the courses that they deliver, the industries that they serve and the sort of faculty that they bring in.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of our IHLs are very research intensive and some of our IHLs are far more focused on practice professorships, for example.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the promotion and tenure communities, the way in which the senior governance within the IHLs look at these things for their faculty and for their outcomes, it is customised for their campus, if you like.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have oversight from MOE for how they develop these frameworks, but the frameworks that they have for each campus is suitable for their needs.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I also wonder whether my COS speech for MCCY has somehow been leaked, so the short answer to the Member's question is yes, there is room for MOE to work more closely together with the High Performance Sport Institute, and all the national sports associations, when it comes to nurturing that love and to be able to collaborate well, use some of the existing criteria and promotion frameworks to really do more for our student athletes.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, I do not want to let the cat out of the bag too soon, but I will be elaborating a lot more in my MCCY COS speech.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The short answer is yes, we will work closer to make sure that our students get better benefits.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One is pertaining to what Senior Minister of State Janil has shared about MySkillsFuture Portal, revamping it.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can we explore to actually allow the functions for the users to actually navigate through the portal based on locations wise, so that it allows the users to benefit from it.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is aligned to my earlier cuts in relation to supporting people, for example, like stay home mothers, people with mobility issues to get closer to enhance and embrace lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is in relation to, also back to my cuts about exploring to have ITE or lifelong learning centre in the north.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is actually a very practical suggestion, especially since we have existing infrastructures available once the sports school moves out and moves to Kallang, so this is something that I really hope that MOE can consider.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Currently, users can filter on the basis of training provider, which may be a proxy for location as well, but I take the Member's point that perhaps this is another way in which we can improve the search experience and I thank her for her suggestion.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I hear from him that from June onwards, the MTLLPC will be introducing and working with communities for parent workshops.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask on the number of locations identified?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: How were they identified and whether Nee Soon South will be considered, because it also has a relatively high proportion of young family in the population?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: My second question, on a serious note, I would like to ask the teacher, Minister, for clarification on my answer to his PSLE question.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: My cortisol levels are spiking and overflowing, so I hope to get an answer from him as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: With regard to the details as to where in the different communities we will be engaging, I think it is still being developed in terms of the details, but certainly if Nee Soon South is keen to be able to engage MOE to develop programmes in keeping with the development of the MTLs, we can discuss that in further detail.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Lee, do you want to reveal the answer?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is really to demonstrate that with scaffolding, it helps to build on the students' understanding of basic concepts, and then stretch and apply it in an environment and in a situation that they may not be familiar with.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First, I would like to thank the Minister for my five marks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For Minister of State Jasmin on AI, I welcome the framework of the four “Learns”, but if I could seek some clarity.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand that she had earlier shared that the guidelines have been sent to all schools and for teachers to introduce it.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Minister of State share the staging and the levels by which, even if broadly, when students would be encouraged or be introduced to AI?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because beyond the four “Learns”, I think there is, to me, another factor.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And that is learning before AI, so that students have a firm basis in knowledge, in mastery of gathering information before AI comes into play.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second related question is that now that we have engaged the teaching community in schools, as well as introducing to students, there is another important group of stakeholders, and that is parents.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because just now we keep mentioning arms race, and I think as parents ourselves, sometimes, it is prone that when we are worried that something new is introduced, we would want to enter an AI tools arms race and end up spurring another round of worry for students' ability to cope as well as a differentiation in between different levels of students – those who have more and those who have less.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: At the secondary level, I think that is where students must move on from awareness to responsible use, so they will be exposed to the tools and learn how to use them to generate ideas, compare perspectives or refine their arguments and, of course, at the post-secondary and the IHL level, they will have to learn how AI tools can be applied to their own discipline, their domain of work and also understand how these translate into real world skills that they will then use when they enter the workforce.

speaker: The Chairman
text: One last clarification, Dr Hamid Razak, for your two cuts and four minutes.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: First, I would like to ask the Minister, I welcome the move to move away from GEP to the 15 centres for advanced modules, whether the Ministry has assessed whether this will then portray these centres as the more choicier schools to parents and how the communication should be better informed so that the parents know the intent of these centres providing the advanced modules?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: To Senior Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun, I do agree that there is no one-size-fits approach for Mother Tongue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these schools provide the infrastructure for these centres to run the modules.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The centres will be reviewed from time to time for geographical spread as well as convenience and access to transport.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Indeed, we do want our MTLs to be as accessible as possible, especially to our students who may have different inclinations as well as different abilities in the MTLs.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, at the level of primary school I mentioned there is a foundation MTL for those who may find themselves a bit weaker.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: We also have G1, G2 MTLs in secondary school, but at the other end, we also want to be able to stretch those who have the potential and ability in Mother Tongue.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: For those who want to further their studies, they can also go on to the language elective programme.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, to answer the Member's question, we do have different types of curricula to be able to allow for different abilities in our students and the intent is for them to be able to appreciate and learn to love the language of their own Mother Tongue at depth and to as high level as possible.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It allowed 11 Members to ask their clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Having said that, being succinct does not mean speaking at a breakneck speed.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It is tough for the Minister to understand, and it is also tough for our interpreters to do their translations.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can I invite Mr Darryl David if you would like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I ask for leave to withdraw my cut.
